name: ProstT5 + Foldseek
compares: Shape letters (3Di) predicted from the amino-acid sequence by the ProstT5 protein language model, then searched with Foldseek, so no AlphaFold model is needed.
reference: 3Di letters predicted by ProstT5 for the relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), as a Foldseek database.
score: Bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
caveats: Proteins longer than 6,000 residues are skipped before the 3Di letters are predicted, and are listed in a skipped-proteins file.

Predicting the 3Di letters ran on one GPU (foldseek createdb --gpu 1). For the 998 queries that step is counted in the GPU column and the cost; for each relative's proteome it is a one-off database build and is not counted.

known_failure_modes.finding: Aligner calls run past the domain, because a call spans the whole aligned stretch. Over correct calls, they start a median 5 to 21 residues early. Over all calls, 45% to 60% start more than 100 residues early.
known_failure_modes.number: median 5 to 21 residues early; 45% to 60% more than 100 residues early

evidence.quote: Over correct calls, the median of call start minus true start is 0 for hmmscan, whose models define the Pfam truth, so the 1-based reading of truth and aligners holds. Aligners start a median 5 to 21 residues early, because a call spans the whole aligned stretch.
45% to 60% of aligner calls start more than 100 residues early, not "most"

known_failure_modes.run: `make leaderboard-pileup` and the region pile-up page (Figure 4)
known_failure_modes.what_to_do: Read a call's ends as the alignment's ends, not the domain's. To score where a domain sits, place the target's domain through the alignment.

commercial_use: Yes. Foldseek's GPL-3.0 applies to changed versions you distribute.
command:
foldseek createdb filtered.fasta zebrafish_prostt5/db \
    --prostt5-model weights --gpu 1 --threads 8

foldseek search \
    human-38fdd87d_prostt5/db zebrafish_prostt5/db result tmp \
    --threads 16 \
    -e 10.0 \
    --max-seqs 1000
questions: Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.139 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.209 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.247 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.144 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (435 Mya) as the relative searched, setting shape letters from sequence; subsets with at least 30 true instances.)
Do you have a GPU to predict the 3Di letters for your proteins? The run used one GPU for that step; its cost is not counted here.
Can you spend about 0.109 core-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured mean per relative; see "Cost per 1,000 queries" below.
